name: stateful-sessionizer
context: Raw telemetry arrives as sparse, individually meaningless events with no session identifier — page views, API calls, heartbeats. Sessionization reconstructs periods of activity per entity: events separated by less than an inactivity gap belong to one session, events beyond the gap start a new one. Because an arriving event can extend or merge an existing session rather than merely append to it, sessionization is a genuinely merging, stateful operation and not a window type that can be substituted in place of a fixed window.
benefits: Produces a business-meaningful unit of analysis (a visit, a work session, a drive) that no fixed window can express
Session identity survives irregular event timing — a user active for 3 minutes then 2 minutes is one session, not two
Session-level metrics (visits, conversions per visit, funnel abandonment) become computable from unlabelled event streams
Re-keying events to a stable session id enables downstream joins and grouping by visit rather than by clock interval
Dynamic per-event gap extraction lets the session boundary adapt to entity behaviour such as page type or action
tradeoffs: Windows are variable-length and mutually merging, so the store must support merge operations rather than fixed-range keys
Results are corrected after emission — a late event can extend a session already sent downstream, so consumers must upsert, not append
Merging triggers and merging aggregate functions are mandatory; a non-merging configuration silently produces wrong session aggregates
Late events can bridge the gap between two previously unmerged sessions, causing a late firing and a further merge
The gap parameter dominates every session metric, and session counts are extremely sensitive to it — the metric is an artefact of the choice
use_cases: Clickstream analytics: visits, unique visitors, pages per session, conversion funnels per session
Application performance: grouping a user's API calls into sessions separated by inactivity
IoT and industrial telemetry: grouping device messages into operational sessions around an activity window
Security analytics: detecting a burst of failed actions followed by inactivity within one session
Network and database telemetry: reconstructing client sessions from connection-level records
avoid_when: The business question is a fixed-interval aggregate — tumbling windows are simpler and cheaper
The source already carries a session or transaction identifier, making reconstruction unnecessary
Entities can be active indefinitely without a meaningful notion of 'ended' — no gap can close those sessions
Late data is not tolerable and the source cannot be made more timely; merging corrections would be unbounded
component_types: Session window assigner: assigns each element to a session defined by an inactivity gap, static or dynamically extracted per element
Gap extractor: per-element function returning the inactivity threshold for that record
Session store: state type that can hold multiple overlapping candidate sessions per key and merge them
Merging window function: aggregate capable of combining two partially-accumulated session aggregates
Merging trigger: fires on both element arrival and window merge, merging trigger state alongside window state
Late-event handler: re-opens and re-merges sessions when a late element bridges a gap
technology_stack: Apache Spark Structured Streaming (session window assignor)
anti_patterns: Using session windows where a tumbling window would answer the question, paying merge cost for nothing
Choosing the inactivity gap from one observed histogram rather than from a distribution across the full population
Materialising session results into a downstream store that only appends, so merge corrections arrive as duplicates
Ignoring that a late event can bridge two previously separate sessions and emit a corrected result downstream
Storing sessions in a fixed-range window store, which cannot represent variable-length merging windows
design_principles: Inactivity defines the boundary, not the calendar
Sessions merge, they do not merely grow — every state structure must support combination
Session identity is an output, not an input
Corrections are expected downstream; the contract is upsert
The gap is a product decision with statistical consequences, recorded alongside the metric definition
best_practices: Derive the gap from the inter-arrival distribution so the chosen value separates real sessions from noise
Require a merging trigger and a merging window function; session windows are evaluated differently from fixed windows
Emit session ids as first-class output so downstream consumers can group without re-implementing sessionization
Treat every downstream write as an upsert keyed by session id
Monitor late-event rate — a rising rate means the gap or the watermark tolerance is mis-set
references: Apache Kafka, Streams DSL — Session Windows and sessionization, https://kafka.apache.org/43/streams/developer-guide/dsl-api/
Apache Flink, Windows — session windows, dynamic gaps, merging triggers and late firings, https://nightlies.apache.org/flink/flink-docs-stable/docs/dev/datastream/operators/windows/
